title: Word Scramble Game
story: The letters appear on screen, shuffled into chaos: 'NOYTHP'. Your brain churns. Five seconds later: 'PYTHON!' You're not just playing a word game — you BUILT it. Pick a random word from the bank, scramble the letters with a shuffle algorithm, show a hint when the player is stuck, track their score across rounds, and celebrate each victory. You are both the game designer and the game engine.
why: Word Scramble combines Vec for letter manipulation, random for word selection and shuffling, Map for word bank storage, structs for game state, and hint logic — a complete interactive word game.
analogy: A jar of alphabet soup. Someone poured in the letters of 'PYTHON' but stirred them up. You stare at 'NOYTHP' and try to mentally un-stir them back into the word. Your shuffle algorithm IS the spoon — it stirs the letters randomly. The player's job is to reverse-engineer the original word. Hints are like seeing the first letter float to the top of the soup.
try_it: Add difficulty levels: Easy (4-5 letter words), Medium (6-8 letters), Hard (9+ letters). Add a timed mode: the player has 30 seconds per word. Add streaks: 3 correct in a row = 2x points. Add a 'used words' set to avoid repeating words in the same session. Add multiple rounds with a final score summary.
tips: Shuffle by picking random indices from the source Vec and removing them — Fisher-Yates style
Score should reward: correct guess (100), no hints (+20), word length (+5 per letter), speed
Hint should give just enough: first letter + word length = big clue without revealing
common_mistakes: Shuffle producing a result identical to the original word — rare but possible, re-shuffle if same
Case sensitivity: 'Python' vs 'PYTHON' won't match — normalize to uppercase in word bank
Removing from Vec while iterating forward — removal shifts indices, use while .len() > 0 pattern
